successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: Qingtang, renamed Xining, annexed from Tsongkha in 1103

ledger.x: 997: 'The elders of Amdo found a Yarlung descendant in Gaochang and took him to Hezhou'.
1032: the court 'relocated to Qingtang' (Xining) after a move to Miaochuan in 1025; his sons 'took Hezhou and Tsongkha'.
1065: Gusiluo dies and Dongzhan succeeds; 'Mucheng declared independence in Hezhou and sided with the Tanguts'.
1072: 'Wang Shao attacked Mucheng and gained control of Wushengjun (Xizhou) and Hezhou'.
1072: Hezhou goes to the Song ('Wang Shao... gained control of Wushengjun (Xizhou) and Hezhou'); the Song dossier records the matching gain.

1099: 'Xiazheng expelled by Xinmouqinzhan, Longza enthroned, Song commander Wang Shan defeated Longza and occupied Tsongkha'; the Gusiluo page: 'In 1099, the Northern Song launched a campaign into Xining and Haidong'.
1103: 'the Song dispatched Wang Hou to conquer Tsongkha'; Xishelosa fled west toward Qinghai.
1103: the kingdom ends in the Song conquest.

wars.name: Song-Tsongkha war of 1017
wars.outcome: Tsongkha was 'defeated by the Song commander Cao Wei' in 1017; the page gives no land change.

wars.name: Xihe campaign against Mucheng
wars.outcome: Wang Shao 'gained control of Wushengjun (Xizhou) and Hezhou' in 1072; in 1074 Dongzhan and Mucheng submitted to Song governance.

wars.name: Song conquest of Tsongkha
wars.outcome: 1099 Wang Shan defeated Longza and occupied Tsongkha; 1103 Wang Hou conquered the kingdom and Qingtang became Xining.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary, an area or a map for Tsongkha; every region is a disc round a place the page names (confidence 1), apart from the dated losses of Hezhou (1072) and Qingtang (1103).
